clue.text: Black headgear for some cops and some cricketers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the round black hard hats once worn by some plain-clothes detectives
second meaning: the players who deliver the ball in cricket

explanation.surface: A note on the dark hats worn by certain policemen and certain cricket players.
explanation.walkthrough: A bowler is a rounded black felt hat, long associated with City gents and detectives; in cricket the bowler delivers the ball to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun names both the felt hats and the cricket players who deliver the ball.

clue.text: Statuesque sheep, for example, all the same?

parts.note: sheep are an example of livestock, or stock
still can mean nevertheless, all the same

explanation.surface: A sheep standing motionless as a statue, the way they all seem to look identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Something statuesque is motionless like a sculpture, which is the sense of the hyphenated adverb or adjective.

clue.text: Starters for All Blacks look extremely talented

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so only the opening letter of each following word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: New Zealand's rugby team, the All Blacks, are looking supremely gifted from kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The All Blacks are New Zealand's rugby union team, named for their black kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone talented is skilled and capable, a straightforward synonym for this short adjective.

clue.text: Movie with traditionally distinctive headgear we back

parts.note: taken as written
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone backing a film famous for its characteristic hats.
explanation.walkthrough: In classic cowboy films the hero wore a white hat and the villain a black one, which ties the definition to the puzzle's black-and-white theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy film set on the American frontier is a genre whose good and bad characters were told apart by hat colour.

clue.text: Like Mont Blanc, with cow wandering into shot

indicators.note: something wandering moves about aimlessly, so the letters of cow drift out of order
into tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: snapped means photographed, shot with a camera
the letters of cow rearranged

explanation.surface: An Alpine snapshot spoiled when a cow strays into the frame in front of Mont Blanc.
explanation.walkthrough: Mont Blanc, the highest Alp, has a permanently white summit; its name means white mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mont Blanc's summit is permanently covered in white, so the mountain has a top crowned with frozen precipitation.

clue.text: Singular white bird that's rarely black

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
wan means pale, white-faced

explanation.surface: A lone white bird of a kind that is only seldom found in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White bird' looks like the definition, but white is only pale; black swans exist, mostly in Australia, which makes them rare elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Most of these long-necked waterbirds are white, with the dark Australian species the exception.

clue.text: Hard cheese dished up initially with black spread

indicators.note: spread suggests letters scattered about and laid out in a new order
initially points to the first letter of each of the two words just before it

parts.note: the first letters of dished and up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm cheese served with a dark spread, as if a dish at a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese' is British slang for misfortune, said with little sympathy; here it is the definition, not something served.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom hard cheese is an offhand way of commiserating over misfortune, the same as saying tough luck.

clue.text: Starts off one risky transaction in black, ready to divide into groups

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another word

parts.note: sable is a heraldic and poetic word for black

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the first letters of one, risky and transaction

explanation.surface: A gambler beginning a risky deal while still in the black, poised to split assets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In black' reads as being in credit, but black here is the heraldic colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be classified or arranged by kind is capable of being placed into categories.

clue.text: Cardinal recently appointed black or white bishop, say

parts.note: someone recently appointed is new to the job
a chess bishop is an example of a man, a piece in the game

explanation.surface: A churchman newly raised to cardinal from bishop, either of the black or white sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' tempts us to stay with the clergy, but it is a chess piece, which players call a man.
explanation.definitionFit: John Henry Newman was a famous Victorian churchman made a prince of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Most tragic need in defeat

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: to best someone is to defeat them
a need is a lack of something

explanation.surface: Losing at a time of great want is the saddest thing of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Defeat is a verb here, as in to get the better of someone, not the noun it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Black can mean gloomy or calamitous, so the superlative describes the bleakest, saddest outcome.

clue.text: Manipulate position after white's opening

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of white
an angle is a position or standpoint

explanation.surface: A chess player rearranging a position following white's first move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the position second; 'white's opening' sounds like a chess opening but is just the first letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate a situation craftily or obtain something by scheming is a colloquial verb of trickery.

clue.text: One who sits obsessively writing letters in square

definitions.text: One who sits obsessively writing letters in square

parts.words: One who sits obsessively writing letters in square
parts.note: surface reading: a compulsive correspondent, perhaps a letter-writer seated in a town square
setter's reading: filling single letters into the squares of a grid, a habit the solver shares

explanation.surface: A compulsive letter-writer camped out in a public square.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters means alphabetic characters, not correspondence, and the square is a grid cell, so the clue describes the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on puzzles spends hours entering characters into each cell of a grid.

clue.text: White container we put outside in prison

indicators.note: put outside tells us one word wraps around the next one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the cooler is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Prisoners being told to set a pale-coloured box outside the jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' here is white wine, not a colour; the cooler is slang for a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilled bucket or cabinet keeps bottles of white wine cold, so it holds the white.

clue.text: Like Labrador, as opposed to 5?

parts.note: surface reading: describing the Canadian region of Labrador, compared with a snowy peak
setter's reading: a black Labrador dog's coat set against the white top of 5

explanation.surface: Contrasting the Canadian territory of Labrador with Mont Blanc's snowy summit.
explanation.walkthrough: Labrador is the dog, often black-coated, and 5 refers to the white peak in 5 down; the contrast is black top against white top.
explanation.definitionFit: A black Labrador has a coat of deep colour, unlike a summit whose top is white.

clue.text: Some players' forte, oddly — its key components are black and white

definitions.text: Some players' forte, oddly — its key components are black and white

parts.note: surface reading: the thing some performers excel at; oddly because the word for this instrument also means soft, the opposite of forte

parts.words: its key components are black and white
parts.note: setter's reading: the keyboard of this instrument is made of black and white keys

explanation.surface: Musicians' strong suit is, strangely, something whose essential parts are black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument's name is also the musical term for soft, the opposite of forte, which is why it is oddly some players' forte.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianists specialise in this keyboard instrument, whose ivories and ebonies are white and black keys.

clue.text: Old district that's frequently created 20

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a district is a part of a town or region

explanation.surface: An old neighbourhood often captured in monochrome photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 across is IN BLACK AND WHITE; optical art of the 1960s, such as Bridget Riley's early work, often used only those two colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical art makes illusions of movement with stark patterns, many of them painted purely in two contrasting tones.

clue.text: Game which ends with white dispatching black

definitions.text: Game which ends with white dispatching black

parts.words: Game which ends with white dispatching black
parts.note: surface reading: a chess game won by the white player defeating black
setter's reading: the white cue ball potting the black ball, the last ball in a frame

explanation.surface: A chess match won by the white side.
explanation.walkthrough: Black and white sound like chess sides, but in this cue game the white cue ball pots the black, the final colour, to end the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: This cue sport on a large table finishes when the last coloured ball is potted.

clue.text: Gets ready for gathering in white nuts

indicators.note: gathering in means taking something inside, so one word holds another

parts.note: cashes means turns into ready money; ready is slang for cash
W is the abbreviation for white, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: Someone preparing to pick white nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside CASHE-S. 'Gets ready' looks like preparing, but ready is slang for money, so it means converts to cash.
explanation.definitionFit: These kidney-shaped tropical kernels are a common type of edible nut, sold roasted or raw.

clue.text: Play game for two

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Shakespeare's tragedy about the Moor of Venice
second meaning: a board game for two players using black and white counters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play game' reads as a single instruction, but the words split into two nouns; the board game is better known in the US as Reversi.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names both Shakespeare's tragedy and a two-player strategy game whose discs are black on one side and white on the other.

clue.text: Home sides in some games recorded on paper

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
in chess and draughts the two sides are black and white

explanation.surface: Home teams in certain matches have their results written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' sounds like football teams, but here they are the opposing colours in board games.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to print, black ink on white paper, so it means written down formally.

clue.text: American rock-and-roller's piece to play, combining two numbers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Fats, the New Orleans singer and pianist of the 1950s

definitions.text: piece to play, combining two numbers
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a black tile with white spots showing two numbers, one on each half

explanation.surface: A rock-and-roll musician's song combining two numbers into one performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Piece and numbers look musical, but the piece is a game tile and the numbers are its spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Domino was a famous American rock-and-roll pianist, and the game tile carries two spot counts on its face.

clue.text: I advance after securing a major role in 19

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly, so the words around it enclose another letter

parts.note: I taken as written, and advance means go forward
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor moving forward after landing a big part in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside I-GO. 19 is OTHELLO, in which this villain is the ensign who deceives the Moor.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheming ensign in Shakespeare's tragedy has more lines than the title character, a major part.

clue.text: Male joining females in white, typically, in part of Scotland

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
brides are women who typically wear white at weddings

explanation.surface: A man joins women dressed in white somewhere in Scotland, like a wedding in the Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: These island groups off Scotland's west coast form a region of the country.

clue.text: Vivacity of performance in part of noir blockbuster elevated

indicators.note: elevated means raised up, and in a down clue reading upwards runs the letters backwards
in part of means the letters lie inside a stretch of the following words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of noir and the start of blockbuster

explanation.surface: Praise for the spirited acting in a big-budget film noir.
explanation.walkthrough: OIRB, read upwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical and theatrical term means verve or spirit, especially lively energy in playing.

clue.text: Black bird that transported Darwin

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark bird that once carried Darwin, like a winged steed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black bird' looks like a blackbird, but black is just B.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Beagle was the naval survey ship on which Charles Darwin made his famous voyage.

clue.text: Problem for plant that could be why I left

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters that follow might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone explaining they quit because of a garden pest problem.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny sap-sucking insect is a common pest that damages greenhouse and garden plants.
